entries.def: - more evil evil, wicked, painful, harmful

πόνος, -ου, ὁ
[in LXX for עָמָל, etc. ;] 
__1. labour, toil: Col.4.13 
__2. The consequence of toil, distress, suffering, pain (Xen., al., LXX): Rev.16.10-11; 21.4.†
SYN.: see: κόπος (AS)
from Pontus, Pontic , (Iliad by Homer) δένδρεον, probably, the bird-cherry , (Herdotus Historicus) (ML)

Πόντιος, -ου, ὁ 
Pontius, the prænomen of Pilate (see: Πειλᾶτος), Mat.27.2 (Rec., WH, mg.), Luk.3.1, Act.4.27, 1Ti.6.13.†
(AS)

Πόντος, -ου, ὁ 
Pontus, a region of Asia Minor, bordering on the πόντος Εὔξεινος: Act.2.9, 1Pe.1.1.†
(AS)

πορεία, -ας, ἡ
(πορεύω), [in LXX chiefly for הֲלִיכָה and cogn. forms ;] 
__1. a journey: Luk.13.22. 
__2. a going: metaphorically ("the rich man perishes while he is still on the move," Hort., in l), Jas.1.11.†
(AS)

πορεύω, 
(πόρος, a ford, a passage), [in LXX chiefly for הלךְ ;] 
in cl. (the act. becomes obsolete in late Gk.; see M, Pr., 162), to cause to go over, carry, convey. Mid. (always in LXX and NT), ־ομαι, to go, proceed, go on one's way: with accusative, ὁδόν, Act.8.39 before ἐκεῖθεν, Mat.19.15 ἐντεῦθεν, Luk.13.31 ἀπό, Mat.25.41, Luk.4.42; εἰς, Mat.2.20, Mrk.16.12, Luk.1.39, Jhn.7.35, al; εἰς εἰρήνην (cf. 1Ki.1.17).…

πορθέω collat. form (in cl. chiefly poët.) of πέρθω, 
[in LXX: 4Ma.4.23 4Mac.11.4 * ;] 
to destroy, ravage: Act.9.21, Gal.1.13, 23.†
(AS)
